Every call takes the time as an argument, so a test passes any time it likes and gets the same answer on every machine, and a replay driven by the recording's own clock reproduces the same decisions the live supervisor made. We also chose to let the robot resume by itself once both inputs are fresh again, rather than latching the stop until an operator clears it, and wrote that choice down as a decision, not a default.

c.v: Each rule has a reason. The TurtleBot's DiffDrive system publishes odometry 30 times a second,

, so 250 ms is about seven missed messages: long enough to ride out a late one, and short enough that a robot at 0.2 m/s covers about 6 cm before the stop goes out. Commands come from a controller at 20 Hz, or from

while you test by hand, so 500 ms covers five missed commands at the slower rate. The command rule is the one that answers the robot-world problem: without it, a controller that dies after sending 0.2 m/s leaves the robot driving while odometry flows normally. It is also why the stop comes from a timer. When the commands go stale, no command arrives, so no command callback would ever run to stop the robot.
The age is measured from when a message arrived on the supervisor's clock, not from the time stamp in its header, for three reasons. A stamp can be zero:
fills a header only when asked to, and the fake inputs below publish
. A stamp can come from the recording, as in a replay without

. And a stamp is on the publisher's clock, while the arrival time is on the supervisor's own, which is the clock its timeouts are defined on. A clock that jumps back comes from a simulation that was reset or a bag that starts again, and the ROS 2 design article on clocks requires code on ROS time to cope with it. Treating it as stale fails safe: the next message makes the input fresh again. The stop repeats rather than going out once, so a lost stop message is replaced 50 ms later. And the supervisor resumes by itself when both inputs are fresh again. A real robot often latches the stop until an operator clears it. """Starts the Test Bench world with the supervisor between /cmd_vel_nav and the robot."""
import os

from ament_index_python.packages import get_package_share_directory
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch.actions import DeclareLaunchArgument, IncludeLaunchDescription
from launch.launch_description_sources import PythonLaunchDescriptionSource
from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration
from launch_ros.actions import Node


def generate_launch_description():
    world = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            os.path.join(get_package_share_directory('bench_sim'), 'launch', 'world.launch.py')),
        launch_arguments={'headless': LaunchConfiguration('headless')}.items())
    supervisor = Node(package='bench_nodes', executable='supervisor',
                      parameters=[{'use_sim_time': True}], output='screen')
    return LaunchDescription([
        DeclareLaunchArgument('headless', default_value='True'),
        world,
        supervisor,
    ])
